us-nv-ut-id-p4-novva-utah-page-20260910.summary: Novva's Utah page says 'Our accessible, sustainable, safe, and secure Utah data center is located near Salt Lake City in West Jordan, UT' and calls it its flagship data center, 'spanning 100 acres with 1.5 million square feet of purpose-built data center space'. It publishes 2025 monthly water usage reports and states 'Novva uses ~394,667 gallons/month (4.7 million gallons/year)'; its specifications list an annualized PUE of 1.18, on-site 24x7 staffing, a 100% uptime SLA, 200,000 sq ft of white floor space, an on-site 200 MW substation, waterless cooling and four purpose-built data centers in a four-phase development (the FAQ says the 1.5 million sq ft is 'planned across a four-phase development'), and the FAQ says the campus 'is built for performance today and expansion tomorrow'. These present-tense statements (water use measured and reported with 2025 monthly bills, round-the-clock on-site staffing, the flagship-campus description and colocation deployments of 250 kW to 30 MW) describe a data center in service; the annualized PUE of 1.18 is one of the listed specifications.
